sentences.text: Researchers investigated whether treating bone marrow cells with EGF could protect against brain damage in a rat model of neurodegeneration. Forty rats were divided into four groups, including a control group and those receiving cells treated with EGF after brain injury was simulated by administering a chemical called trimethyltin chloride.

Scientists measured learning, movement, brain tissue, and protein levels, finding that cells treated with 10 ng/mL of EGF grew into shapes resembling neurons. Rats receiving these modified cells showed better memory and movement skills, while microscopic examination revealed that brain structures in the hippocampus were better preserved. The treatment lowered markers of inflammation and nerve damage while raising levels of factors that support nerve growth and repair.
The authors conclude that this approach might be a promising future treatment for neurodegenerative diseases, though it is currently based on animal findings.
